title: Fix reject_missing_methods returning 500 instead of 405
description:
With `reject_missing_methods = TRUE`, `add_handler()` registers an `"all"` handler that answers wrong-method requests with 405. That handler builds the `Allow` list with `vapply()`, but a misplaced parenthesis put `logical(1)` inside `is.null()`, so `FUN.VALUE` was missing and every wrong-method request errored (500) instead of getting a 405.

The guard just above it also looked up `private$handlerMap`, which doesn't exist on `Route`, so it was always `NULL` and the `"all"` handler was re-registered on every call. It now checks `private$routing`.

Added a test for a POST-only route: GET now returns 405 with `Allow: POST`, and POST still reaches the handler.

This came up in posit-dev/plumber2#86 (`rejectMissingMethods` turning wrong-method requests into 500s) and should fix it there, though I haven't tested through plumber2.

Don't prepend '/' to paths on Windows
description:
On Windows, prepending '/' on `complete_paths` creates invalid paths, e.g.

    > routr:::complete_paths('C:/Users')
    [1] "/C:/Users/"

This commit simply adds a test if R is running on Windows, and if so, the beginning of the path is left untouched.
